title: Finding source of leak is doubtful, analysts say
author: Not specified
thematic_categories: Press & Media Criticism, Journalism Theory & Practice, Politics & Democracy
summary: An article about the difficulty of investigating government leaks, specifically regarding the leak that revealed a CIA operative's identity. Jay Rosen is quoted as a New York University journalism department official discussing the news value of leaks versus the ethics of publishing them.
excerpt: "The problem in cases like this is that there may be certain news value in what the leaker is offering, but there may be more news value in the fact that the person is trying to leak it," said professor Jay Rosen, a New York University journalism department official. "First Amendment values must be more in value in the newsroom than value in the courtroom," Rosen said. "That is a genuine secret: You should keep it secret."
pull_quote: First Amendment values must be more in value in the newsroom than value in the courtroom. That is a genuine secret: You should keep it secret.
